trial_court: Family Court-cum-Additional chief Judge, City Civil Court, F.C.O.P No. 1328 of 2015
case_name: Lingla Nirupama Reddy vs Lingala Venkata Narasimha Reddy
facts_of_case: The Petitioner filed a petition for divorce against the Respondent under Section 13(1) (ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The marriage was consummated but no children were born out of the wedlock. The Respondent tortured the Petitioner over petty issues and demanded additional dowry.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove the same.
legal_principles.held: The petitioner voluntarily withdrew from the company of the respondent, without any justifiable cause and consistently refused to resume cohabitation despite repeated requests and efforts for reconciliation.

legal_principles.principle: A party's refusal to resume cohabitation despite efforts for reconciliation can be a factor in determining the existence of cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The respondent stated to have made sincere attempts for mediation and reunion, whereas the petitioner remained adamant in refusing conjugal companionship.

legal_principles.principle: The absence of a criminal complaint during the subsistence of marriage can indicate that no cruelty occurred.
legal_principles.held: The non-filing of any criminal complaint by the petitioner during the subsistence of marriage, categorically indicates that no cruelty, as alleged, ever occurred.

outcome.result: Appeal disposed of by this common Judgment
outcome.final_order: The petition filed by the Petitioner seeking divorce was dismissed, and the counter claim preferred by the Respondent seeking restitution of conjugal rights was also dismissed.
